content.user_title: Adapt Learning Resources to Academic Domains
content.value_statement: Generic learning resources often miss domain conventions and evidence standards. This skill provides tailored research, terminology, structure, and review guidance for five domains.
actual_capabilities: Maps technology, history, science, arts, and general topics to dedicated profiles.
Provides source priorities and reusable search query patterns for each domain.
Defines domain-specific metadata for environments, timelines, equations, laboratories, materials, and learning needs.
Applies terminology, translation, citation, and first-use formatting policies.
Recommends educational structures with examples, exercises, and progressive difficulty.
Supplies critical, quality, and style checks for reviewing domain content.
limitations: It provides configuration guidance but does not research or write complete resources by itself.
Its source recency examples reference 2024 and 2025, so users must verify current information.
Many examples use Korean and English, requiring localization for other languages.
The fixed domain set needs adaptation for specialized or interdisciplinary subjects.

use_cases.title: Plan Domain Research
use_cases.description: Choose authoritative source types, query patterns, and metadata before collecting evidence.

use_cases.title: Structure Learning Materials
use_cases.description: Organize explanations, examples, exercises, terminology, and citations for a selected subject.

use_cases.title: Review Educational Drafts
use_cases.description: Apply domain-specific critical, quality, and style checks to learning resources.

prompt_templates.title: Select a Domain Profile
prompt_templates.prompt: Classify my topic, {TOPIC}, as technology, history, science, arts, or general. Name the profile and explain the choice.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Research Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the {DOMAIN} profile to create a research plan for {TOPIC}. Include source priorities, search queries, and required metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Learning Outline
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the {DOMAIN} content structure and terminology policy to {TOPIC}. Create an outline for {AUDIENCE} with examples and exercises.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Cross-Domain Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this {PRIMARY_DOMAIN} draft using its critical, quality, and style checks. Add relevant {SECONDARY_DOMAIN} guidance and identify conflicts: {DRAFT}.

output_examples.input: Plan a Python concurrency guide for intermediate developers.
output: Sources: official Python documentation, release notes, and maintained repositories
Structure: motivation, environment setup, basic usage, advanced patterns, project, and troubleshooting
Review focus: runnable examples, error handling, type annotations, version notes, and unsafe pattern checks

output_examples.input: Outline a resource about the causes of the Renaissance.
output: Evidence: primary sources, academic journals, archives, and historiographical reviews
Structure: background, causes, events, perspectives, evidence, impact, and debates
Review focus: citations, chronology, multiple viewpoints, and separation of facts from interpretations

output_examples.input: Review a beginner lesson about Newtonian motion.
output: Check equations, units, symbol definitions, derivation steps, worked examples, and prerequisites.
Require safety notes only when the lesson includes laboratory activities.

best_practices: Select the closest profile before research begins, then document any cross-domain needs.
Verify source currency, factual claims, citations, and safety guidance outside the profile.
Apply critical checks first, followed by quality and style checks.
anti_patterns: Do not treat example sources or dates as verified research results.
Do not combine profiles without resolving conflicting terminology and structure rules.
Do not omit citations, safety notes, or validation because a profile supplies a template.

faq.question: Which domains are included?
faq.answer: The skill includes technology, history, science, arts, and general or language profiles.

faq.question: Does the skill perform web research?
faq.answer: No. It recommends sources and query patterns that another agent or user can follow.

faq.question: Which profile handles general topics?
faq.answer: Use language.md for general topics. A separate general.md profile does not exist.

faq.question: Can I use more than one profile?
faq.answer: Yes. Choose a primary profile and apply only relevant guidance from secondary profiles.

faq.question: Does it generate complete lessons?
faq.answer: No. It supplies planning, structure, terminology, and review guidance for a separate writing workflow.

faq.question: Are the profiles suitable for every language?
faq.answer: The principles are reusable, but many examples use Korean and English. Other languages require localization.
